critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/utils/overseas_share.py — clean single-source-of-truth helper. is_overseas() defensively normalizes country casing/whitespace; compute_overseas_share() rounds at 2dp; compute_cumulative_mfpl() walks daily_sales month-by-month via compute_gst_from_rows so MFPL accrual stays canonical with the GST module. Constants OWNER_PCT=80 / FRANCHISOR_PCT=20 / MFPL_ROYALTY_PCT=5 are file-level and importable.

Defensive max(0.0, …) on eligible_profit prevents negative-profit shares from appearing as 'Owner share' obligations — good (loss months simply yield AUD 0 share which is the right business semantics).

paid_mfpl is hardcoded to 0.0 in compute_cumulative_mfpl; the 'Future:' comment correctly anticipates a payment-tracking collection. Once payments are tracked, outstanding = cumulative − paid will Just Work.

Audit script audit_financial_parity.py correctly skips the India-only 'Eligible Rev Share Base == Net Revenue' check for AU (`if owner.get('country','India') != 'Australia'`) — preserves cross-country parity audit without false positives.
PIB generator and FO Ledger PDF both render for PERTH without errors (>50KB output) — confirms the overseas branch is wired through pdf_generator and ledgers.py builders.

rca_of_the_issue: Not a bug — this iteration added a new feature: overseas (non-India) franchise economics. The implementation correctly bifurcates by country: overseas centers get a fixed 80/20 profit share on Eligible Profit (Sales − GST − Commission − CommGST − Expenses) with a 5% MFPL royalty accrued cumulatively as a liability (paid=0 always for now), and explicitly NO MG. India centers retain the existing MG vs Revenue Share logic. The financial parity audit confirms numerical agreement across every surface (Center Accounts, Owner Reports, MIS, Payout Summary, WC table) for both an overseas (PB-PERTH) and an Indian (PB-HSR) center in the same period.
